newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia aluminium juniors unite with bigger players.
newsitem.headline: Russia aluminium juniors unite with bigger players.

text.p: A host of Russia's junior aluminium producers plan to join forces with a few of the bigger domestic plants to form a company to streamline production and financial issues, Interfax news agency said on Monday.

The new firm, to be called Integrated Aluminium Corporation, or Interalco, would include Trans-Consult Group, the Siberian-Urals Aluminium Company (uniting the Urals and Irkutsk smelters), and the Bogoslovsky, Novokuznetsk, Volgograd and Kandalaksha smelters.
It would also include the Yuzhno-Uralsky bauxite mines and other secondary metallurgical factories.
Interfax said Interalco might bring on board foreign investors, but it gave no details on how the new company would function or what it planned.
Smelters in Russia, the world's largest primary aluminium exporter, are seeking vertical integration to cut costs and streamline production processes.
The biggest smelters -- Bratsk, Krasnoyarsk -- were not mentioned as being part of the group.

The Irkutsk smelter, one of four in southern Siberia, has an annual primary aluminium capacity of around 250,000 tonnes. The Urals plant can produce around 100,000 tonnes a year, while Bogoslovsky can do around 150,000 tonnes.
Novokuznetsk's annual capacity is around 250,000 tonnes, Volgograd's is 160,000 tonnes, and Kandalaksha's is 65,000 tonnes.
Russia's primary aluminium exports last year were 2.44 million tonnes from domestic output of 2.87 million tonnes.
Capacities of smelters in the new corporation would account for about one-third of Russia's total 1996 output.
